sanskrit: patitāṃs tomarāṃś cāpi citrā hemapariṣkṛtāḥ kuthāś ca bahudhākārāś cāmaravyajanāni ca
english: There lay fallen lances too, and gay caparisons wrought with gold of many shapes, and fans made of yak-tail whisks.

sanskrit: nānāvidhāni śastrāṇi visṛjya patitā narāḥ jīvanta iva dṛśyante gatasattvā mahārathāḥ
english: Having let fall their weapons of every kind, the men lay there; and the great chariot-warriors, though their breath was gone, seemed as if still living.

sanskrit: gadāvimathitair gātrair musalair bhinnamastakāḥ gajavājirathakṣuṇṇāḥ śerate sma narāḥ kṣitau
english: Their limbs crushed by maces, their skulls split open by clubs, trampled by elephants, horses, and chariots, the men lay strewn upon the earth.

sanskrit: tathaivāśvanṛnāgānāṃ śarīrair ābabhau tadā saṃchannā vasudhā rājan parvatair iva sarvataḥ
english: And so with the bodies of horses, men, and elephants the earth then shone, O king, covered over on every side as though with mountains.

sanskrit: samare patitaiś caiva śaktyṛṣṭiśaratomaraiḥ nistriṃśaiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ prāsair ayaskuntaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ
english: With spears, darts, arrows, and lances fallen in the fray, with swords, spiked maces, javelins, iron pikes, and battle-axes,

sanskrit: parighair bhiṇḍipālaiś ca śataghnībhis tathaiva ca śarīraiḥ śastrabhinnaiś ca samāstīryata medinī
english: with bludgeons, slings, and engines that slay a hundred, and with bodies cleft by weapons, the earth was overspread.

sanskrit: niḥśabdair alpaśabdaiś ca śoṇitaughapariplutaiḥ gatāsubhir amitraghna vibabhau saṃvṛtā mahī
english: Strewn with the dead — some voiceless, some scarcely moaning, all bathed in floods of blood — the earth shone forth, O slayer of foes, covered with the lifeless.

sanskrit: satalatraiḥ sakeyūrair bāhubhiś candanokṣitaiḥ hastihastopamaiś chinnair ūrubhiś ca tarasvinām
english: With arms still bearing their leather guards and armlets, anointed with sandal, hewn off and like the trunks of elephants, and with the severed thighs of the mighty,

sanskrit: baddhacūḍāmaṇidharaiḥ śirobhiś ca sakuṇḍalaiḥ patitair vṛṣabhākṣāṇāṃ babhau bhārata medinī
english: and with the fallen heads of bull-eyed heroes, bound about with their crest-jewels and still wearing their earrings, the earth shone, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kavacaiḥ śoṇitādigdhair viprakīrṇaiś ca kāñcanaiḥ rarāja subhṛśaṃ bhūmiḥ śāntārcibhir ivānalaiḥ
english: With golden corslets smeared with blood and scattered all about, the ground gleamed exceedingly, as with fires whose flames had died down.

sanskrit: vipraviddhaiḥ kalāpaiś ca patitaiś ca śarāsanaiḥ viprakīrṇaiḥ śaraiś cāpi rukmapuṅkhaiḥ samantataḥ
english: With quivers flung asunder and bows fallen down, and with arrows golden-feathered scattered on every side,

sanskrit: rathaiś ca bahubhir bhagnaiḥ kiṅkiṇījālamālibhiḥ vājibhiś ca hataiḥ kīrṇaiḥ srastajihvaiḥ saśoṇitaiḥ
english: with many chariots broken, garlanded with nets of little bells, and with slain horses strewn about, their tongues lolling out, smeared with blood,

sanskrit: anukarṣaiḥ patākābhir upāsaṅgair dhvajair api pravīrāṇāṃ mahāśaṅkhair viprakīrṇaiś ca pāṇḍuraiḥ
english: with chariot-poles, pennons, quivers, and banners, and with the great white conches of the foremost warriors scattered abroad,

sanskrit: srastahastaiś ca mātaṅgaiḥ śayānair vibabhau mahī nānārūpair alaṃkāraiḥ pramadevābhyalaṃkṛtā
english: and with elephants lying with trunks drooping, the earth shone, decked with ornaments of every shape, like a lovely woman richly adorned.

sanskrit: dantibhiś cāparais tatra saprāsair gāḍhavedanaiḥ karaiḥ śabdaṃ vimuñcadbhiḥ śīkaraṃ ca muhur muhuḥ vibabhau tad raṇasthānaṃ dhamyamānair ivācalaiḥ
english: With other tusked elephants there, pierced by spears and in sore anguish, sending forth cries with their trunks and again and again a spray of foam, that field of battle gleamed as though with mountains being blown upon.

sanskrit: nānārāgaiḥ kambalaiś ca paristomaiś ca dantinām vaiḍūryamaṇidaṇḍaiś ca patitair aṅkuśaiḥ śubhaiḥ
english: With blankets and housings of many hues belonging to the elephants, and with fair goads fallen, their shafts set with beryl gems,

sanskrit: ghaṇṭābhiś ca gajendrāṇāṃ patitābhiḥ samantataḥ vighāṭitavicitrābhiḥ kuthābhī rāṅkavais tathā
english: with the bells of the lordly elephants fallen on every side, and with their gay caparisons torn apart, and with rugs of antelope-hide,

sanskrit: graiveyaiś citrarūpaiś ca rukmakakṣyābhir eva ca yantraiś ca bahudhā chinnais tomaraiś ca sakampanaiḥ
english: with neck-bands of curious make and golden girths, and with engines hacked to pieces, and with lances and javelins,

sanskrit: aśvānāṃ reṇukapilai rukmacchannair uraśchadaiḥ sādināṃ ca bhujaiś chinnaiḥ patitaiḥ sāṅgadais tathā
english: with the breastplates of horses, dust-grey and overlaid with gold, and with the hewn-off arms of riders fallen down, still bearing their armlets,

sanskrit: prāsaiś ca vimalais tīkṣṇair vimalābhis tatharṣṭibhiḥ uṣṇīṣaiś ca tathā chinnaiḥ praviddhaiś ca tatas tataḥ
english: with javelins bright and keen, and with shining darts as well, and with turbans cut off and flung here and there,

sanskrit: vicitrair ardhacandraiś ca jātarūpapariṣkṛtaiḥ aśvāstaraparistomai rāṅkavair mṛditais tathā
english: with gaudy crescent-headed shafts adorned with gold, and with horse-cloths and coverlets of antelope-hide trodden underfoot,

sanskrit: narendracūḍāmaṇibhir vicitraiś ca mahādhanaiḥ chatrais tathāpaviddhaiś ca cāmaravyajanair api
english: with the crest-jewels of kings, curious and of great worth, and with parasols flung aside, and with yak-tail fans,

sanskrit: padmendudyutibhiś caiva vadanaiś cārukuṇḍalaiḥ kḷptaśmaśrubhir atyarthaṃ vīrāṇāṃ samalaṃkṛtaiḥ
english: and with the faces of heroes bright as the lotus and the moon, with lovely earrings and trimmed beards, exceedingly adorned,

sanskrit: apaviddhair mahārāja suvarṇojjvalakuṇḍalaiḥ grahanakṣatraśabalā dyaur ivāsīd vasuṃdharā
english: flung down, O great king, with earrings glittering with gold — the earth became like the sky dappled with planets and stars.

sanskrit: evam ete mahāsene mṛdite tatra bhārata parasparaṃ samāsādya tava teṣāṃ ca saṃyuge
english: Thus, O Bhārata, were those two great hosts ground down there, yours and theirs, when they had closed with one another in the fight.

sanskrit: teṣu śrānteṣu bhagneṣu mṛditeṣu ca bhārata rātriḥ samabhavad ghorā nāpaśyāma tato raṇam
english: And when those men were weary, broken, and worn down, O Bhārata, dread night came on, and we could no longer see the battle.

sanskrit: tato 'vahāraṃ sainyānāṃ pracakruḥ kurupāṇḍavāḥ ghore niśāmukhe raudre vartamāne sudāruṇe
english: Then the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas drew off their armies, while the dread and dire onset of night, fearful to behold, came on.

sanskrit: avahāraṃ tataḥ kṛtvā sahitāḥ kurupāṇḍavāḥ nyaviśanta yathākālaṃ gatvā svaśibiraṃ tadā
english: Having thus withdrawn, the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas together, going each to his own camp, settled down as the hour required.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato duryodhano rājā śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ duḥśāsanaś ca putras te sūtaputraś ca durjayaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then King Duryodhana, and Śakuni the son of Subala, and your son Duḥśāsana, and the invincible son of the charioteer —

sanskrit: samāgamya mahārāja mantraṃ cakrūr vivakṣitam kathaṃ pāṇḍusutā yuddhe jetavyāḥ sagaṇā iti
english: having come together, O great king, took counsel on what they wished to say: how the sons of Pāṇḍu, with their hosts, were to be vanquished in war.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā sarvāṃs tān āha mantriṇaḥ sūtaputraṃ samābhāṣya saubalaṃ ca mahābalam
english: Then King Duryodhana addressed all those counsellors, speaking to the son of the charioteer and to the mighty son of Subala.

sanskrit: droṇo bhīṣmaḥ kṛpaḥ śalyaḥ saumadattiś ca saṃyuge na pārthān pratibādhante na jāne tatra kāraṇam
english: "Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Kṛpa, Śalya, and the son of Somadatta do not press the Pārthas hard in battle — and I do not know the reason for it.

sanskrit: avadhyamānās te cāpi kṣapayanti balaṃ mama so 'smi kṣīṇabalaḥ karṇa kṣīṇaśastraś ca saṃyuge
english: Unslain themselves, the Pāṇḍavas waste away my force; and so, Karṇa, my strength is dwindling and my weapons are spent in the fight.

sanskrit: nikṛtaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ śūrair avadhyair daivatair api so 'haṃ saṃśayam āpannaḥ prakariṣye kathaṃ raṇam
english: Worsted by the heroic Pāṇḍavas, who cannot be slain even by the gods, I am fallen into doubt: how shall I carry on the war?"

sanskrit: tam abravīn mahārāja sūtaputro narādhipam mā śuco bharataśreṣṭha prakariṣye priyaṃ tava
english: To him, O great king, the son of the charioteer answered the lord of men: "Grieve not, O best of the Bharatas; I shall do what pleases you.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavas tūrṇam apayātu mahāraṇāt nivṛtte yudhi gāṅgeye nyastaśastre ca bhārata
english: Let Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, withdraw at once from the great battle; and once the son of Gaṅgā has retired from the fight and laid down his arms, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: ahaṃ pārthān haniṣyāmi sanitān sarvasomakaiḥ paśyato yudhi bhīṣmasya śape satyena te nṛpa
english: I shall slay the Pārthas with all their kin and all the Somakas, before the very eyes of Bhīṣma in battle — this I swear to you by my truth, O king.

sanskrit: pāṇḍaveṣu dayāṃ rājan sadā bhīṣmaḥ karoti vai aśaktaś ca raṇe bhīṣmo jetum etān mahārathān
english: Bhīṣma, O king, ever shows compassion toward the Pāṇḍavas; and Bhīṣma is unable to conquer these great chariot-warriors in battle.

sanskrit: abhimānī raṇe bhīṣmo nityaṃ cāpi raṇapriyaḥ sa kathaṃ pāṇḍavān yuddhe jeṣyate tāta saṃgatān
english: Bhīṣma is proud in war and ever loves the fray; how then, dear lord, shall he conquer the Pāṇḍavas when they stand arrayed in battle?

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ śīghram ito gatvā bhīṣmasya śibiraṃ prati anumānya raṇe bhīṣmaṃ śastraṃ nyāsaya bhārata
english: Do you, then, go swiftly hence to the camp of Bhīṣma, and having won his leave from the battle, make him lay down his arms, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nyastaśastre tato bhīṣme nihatān paśya pāṇḍavān mayaikena raṇe rājan sasuhṛdgaṇabāndhavān
english: When Bhīṣma has laid down his arms, then behold the Pāṇḍavas slain — by me alone in battle, O king, with all their friends, their hosts, and their kinsmen."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu karṇena putro duryodhanas tava abravīd bhrātaraṃ tatra duḥśāsanam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Karṇa, your son Duryodhana spoke this word there to his brother Duḥśāsana:

sanskrit: anuyātraṃ yathā sajjaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati sarvataḥ duḥśāsana tathā kṣipraṃ sarvam evopapādaya
english: "See, Duḥśāsana, that all the retinue is made ready on every side; quickly arrange the whole of it."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rājan karṇam āha janeśvaraḥ anumānya raṇe bhīṣmam ito 'haṃ dvipadāṃ varam
english: Having spoken thus, O king, the lord of men said to Karṇa: "When I have won leave of Bhīṣma in the battle, that best of men,

sanskrit: āgamiṣye tataḥ kṣipraṃ tvatsakāśam ariṃdama tatas tvaṃ puruṣavyāghra prakariṣyasi saṃyugam
english: I shall then come quickly to your side, O subduer of foes; and then, O tiger among men, you shall wage the war."

sanskrit: niṣpapāta tatas tūrṇaṃ putras tava viśāṃ pate sahito bhrātṛbhiḥ sarvair devair iva śatakratuḥ
english: Then your son set forth at once, O lord of peoples, together with all his brothers, like Indra of the hundred sacrifices amid the gods.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ nṛpaśārdūlaṃ śārdūlasamavikramam ārohayad dhayaṃ tūrṇaṃ bhrātā duḥśāsanas tadā
english: Then his brother Duḥśāsana swiftly mounted that tiger among kings, whose valour matched a tiger's, upon his horse.

sanskrit: aṅgadī baddhamukuṭo hastābharaṇavān nṛpaḥ dhārtarāṣṭro mahārāja vibabhau sa mahendravat
english: Wearing armlets, with crown bound on and bracelets upon his arms, the king, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, shone, O great king, like the great Indra.

sanskrit: bhāṇḍīpuṣpanikāśena tapanīyanibhena ca anuliptaḥ parārdhyena candanena sugandhinā
english: Anointed with sandal-paste, fragrant and of priceless worth, glowing like the bhāṇḍī blossom and resembling refined gold,

sanskrit: arajombarasaṃvītaḥ siṃhakhelagatir nṛpaḥ śuśubhe vimalārciṣmañ śaradīva divākaraḥ
english: clad in spotless raiment, moving with the sportive gait of a lion, the king shone bright and radiant, like the sun in autumn.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ naravyāghraṃ bhīṣmasya śibiraṃ prati anujagmur maheṣvāsāḥ sarvalokasya dhanvinaḥ bhrātaraś ca maheṣvāsās tridaśā iva vāsavam
english: As that tiger among men went forth toward the camp of Bhīṣma, the mighty archers, the bowmen of all the world, followed him, and his brothers, great archers all, as the gods follow Vāsava.

sanskrit: hayān anye samāruhya gajān anye ca bhārata rathair anye naraśreṣṭhāḥ parivavruḥ samantataḥ
english: Some mounted on horses, some on elephants, O Bhārata, and others, those best of men, on chariots, surrounded him on every side.

sanskrit: āttaśastrāś ca suhṛdo rakṣaṇārthaṃ mahīpateḥ prādurbabhūvuḥ sahitāḥ śakrasyevāmarā divi
english: And his friends, weapons in hand, gathered together to guard the lord of earth, even as the immortals gather about Śakra in heaven.

sanskrit: saṃpūjyamānaḥ kurubhiḥ kauravāṇāṃ mahārathaḥ prayayau sadanaṃ rājan gāṅgeyasya yaśasvinaḥ anvīyamānaḥ sahitaiḥ sodaraiḥ sarvato nṛpaḥ
english: Honoured by the Kurus, that great chariot-warrior of the Kauravas went on, O king, to the tent of the renowned son of Gaṅgā, the king followed all about by his brothers together.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇaḥ kāle saṃbhṛtya svabhujaṃ tadā hastihastopamaṃ śaikṣaṃ sarvaśatrunibarhaṇam
english: That dexterous prince, raising at the fitting moment his own right arm — well-trained, like the trunk of an elephant, the crusher of every foe —

sanskrit: pragṛhṇann añjalīn nṝṇām udyatān sarvatodiśam śuśrāva madhurā vāco nānādeśanivāsinām
english: received the folded palms of men raised toward him from every quarter, and heard the sweet words of those who dwelt in diverse lands.

sanskrit: saṃstūyamānaḥ sūtaiś ca māgadhaiś ca mahāyaśāḥ pūjayānaś ca tān sarvān sarvalokeśvareśvaraḥ
english: Praised by bards and minstrels, that man of great renown, lord over all the lords of the world, in turn paid honour to them all.

sanskrit: pradīpaiḥ kāñcanais tatra gandhatailāvasecanaiḥ parivavrur mahātmānaṃ prajvaladbhiḥ samantataḥ
english: With golden lamps there, fed with fragrant oil and blazing on every side, they surrounded that high-souled one.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛto rājā pradīpaiḥ kāñcanaiḥ śubhaiḥ śuśubhe candramā yukto dīptair iva mahāgrahaiḥ
english: Encircled by those fair golden lamps, the king shone like the moon attended by the blazing great planets.

sanskrit: kañcukoṣṇīṣiṇas tatra vetrajharjharapāṇayaḥ protsārayantaḥ śanakais taṃ janaṃ sarvatodiśam
english: There the ushers in tunics and turbans, with staves and rattles in their hands, gently moved the throng aside on every quarter.

sanskrit: saṃprāpya tu tato rājā bhīṣmasya sadanaṃ śubham avatīrya hayāc cāpi bhīṣmaṃ prāpya janeśvaraḥ
english: Then, having reached the fair dwelling of Bhīṣma, the king, that lord of men, alighted from his horse and came before Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: abhivādya tato bhīṣmaṃ niṣaṇṇaḥ paramāsane kāñcane sarvatobhadre spardhyāstaraṇasaṃvṛte uvāca prāñjalir bhīṣmaṃ bāṣpakaṇṭho 'śrulocanaḥ
english: Having saluted Bhīṣma, he sat down upon an excellent seat, golden, fair on every side, spread with a priceless covering, and with folded palms, his throat choked with sobs and his eyes brimming with tears, he said to Bhīṣma:

sanskrit: tvāṃ vayaṃ samupāśritya saṃyuge śatrusūdana utsahema raṇe jetuṃ sendrān api surāsurān
english: "Relying upon you in the fray, O slayer of foes, we should dare to conquer in battle even the gods and demons together with Indra —

sanskrit: kim u pāṇḍusutān vīrān sasuhṛdgaṇabāndhavān tasmād arhasi gāṅgeya kṛpāṃ kartuṃ mayi prabho jahi pāṇḍusutān vīrān mahendra iva dānavān
english: how much more the heroic sons of Pāṇḍu, with their friends, their hosts, and their kinsmen! Therefore, O son of Gaṅgā, you should show me your grace, O lord: slay the heroic sons of Pāṇḍu as the great Indra slew the Dānavas.

sanskrit: pūrvam uktaṃ mahābāho nihaniṣyāmi somakān pāñcālān pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ karūṣāṃś ceti bhārata
english: You said before, O mighty-armed one: 'I shall slay the Somakas and the Pāñcālas, together with the Pāṇḍavas and the Karūṣas,' so you spoke, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tad vacaḥ satyam evāstu jahi pārthān samāgatān somakāṃś ca maheṣvāsān satyavāg bhava bhārata
english: Let that word of yours be made true: slay the Pārthas arrayed against us and the Somakas, those mighty archers — be true to your word, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: dayayā yadi vā rājan dveṣyabhāvān mama prabho mandabhāgyatayā vāpi mama rakṣasi pāṇḍavān
english: But if out of compassion, O king, or out of hatred toward me, my lord, or because of my own ill fortune, you spare the Pāṇḍavas,

sanskrit: anujānīhi samare karṇam āhavaśobhinam sa jeṣyati raṇe pārthān sasuhṛdgaṇabāndhavān
english: then give leave in the battle to Karṇa, who is glorious in war; he will conquer in the fight the Pārthas with their friends, their hosts, and their kinsmen."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā nṛpatiḥ putro duryodhanas tava novāca vacanaṃ kiṃ cid bhīṣmaṃ bhīmaparākramam
english: Having said only this much, the king, your son Duryodhana, spoke no further word to Bhīṣma of terrible prowess.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vākśalyais tava putreṇa so 'tividdhaḥ pitāmahaḥ duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭo novācāpriyam aṇv api
english: Saṃjaya said: Though pierced through by your son with those shafts of speech, the grandsire, filled with a great grief, yet spoke not even a trifle that was unkind.

sanskrit: sa dhyātvā suciraṃ kālaṃ duḥkharoṣasamanvitaḥ śvasamāno yathā nāgaḥ praṇunno vai śalākayā
english: For a long while he brooded, filled with grief and wrath, sighing like a serpent goaded with a pointed rod.

sanskrit: udvṛtya cakṣuṣī kopān nirdahann iva bhārata sadevāsuragandharvaṃ lokaṃ lokavidāṃ varaḥ abravīt tava putraṃ tu sāmapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Rolling his eyes in anger, as if to burn up the world with its gods, demons, and gandharvas, O Bhārata, that best of those who know the worlds spoke this word to your son, beginning gently:

sanskrit: kiṃ nu duryodhanaivaṃ māṃ vākśalyair upavidhyasi ghaṭamānaṃ yathāśakti kurvāṇaṃ ca tava priyam juhvānaṃ samare prāṇāṃs tavaiva hitakāmyayā
english: "Why, Duryodhana, do you thus pierce me with shafts of speech, when I am striving to the best of my power and doing what pleases you, offering up my very life in battle out of desire for your good?

sanskrit: yadā tu pāṇḍavaḥ śūraḥ khāṇḍave 'gnim atarpayat parājitya raṇe śakraṃ paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: When the heroic Pāṇḍava, at the Khāṇḍava forest, sated the fire, having vanquished Śakra in battle — that should be proof enough.

sanskrit: yadā ca tvāṃ mahābāho gandharvair hṛtam ojasā amocayat pāṇḍusutaḥ paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: And when you, O mighty-armed one, were carried off by the gandharvas by force, the son of Pāṇḍu set you free — that should be proof enough.

sanskrit: dravamāṇeṣu śūreṣu sodareṣu tathābhibho sūtaputre ca rādheye paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: When the heroes fled — your own brothers, O lord, and the son of the charioteer, Rādheya, with them — that should be proof enough.

sanskrit: yac ca naḥ sahitān sarvān virāṭanagare tadā eka eva samudyātaḥ paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: And when, in the city of Virāṭa, against us all gathered together he rose up single-handed — that should be proof enough.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ ca yudhi saṃrabdhaṃ māṃ ca nirjitya saṃyuge karṇaṃ ca tvāṃ ca drauṇiṃ ca kṛpaṃ ca sumahāratham vāsāṃsi sa samādatta paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: Having overpowered in that battle Droṇa enraged in the fight, and me, and Karṇa, and you, and the son of Droṇa, and Kṛpa, that mighty chariot-warrior, he carried off our garments — that should be proof enough.

sanskrit: nivātakavacān yuddhe vāsavenāpi durjayān jitavān samare pārthaḥ paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: The Nivātakavacas, hard to conquer in battle even by Vāsava, the Pārtha vanquished in the fray — that should be proof enough.

sanskrit: ko hi śakto raṇe jetuṃ pāṇḍavaṃ rabhasaṃ raṇe tvaṃ tu mohān na jānīṣe vācyāvācyaṃ suyodhana
english: For who is able to conquer in battle that Pāṇḍava, impetuous in war? But you, in your delusion, do not know, Suyodhana, what should and should not be said."
